title: Geo‑Residency Aware Permission Sweeper and Evidence Bundles
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers operating under strict data residency and jurisdictional controls need automated detection and remediation for access grants that violate tenant residency or retention policies. Current RBAC and SCIM pipelines surface entitlements but lack an automated way to sweep, flag, or generate tamper-evident artifacts for auditors.

Goal: Ship a cross-tenant "Permission Sweeper" service that continuously evaluates RBAC bindings and SCIM deltas against per-tenant residency metadata and retention policies, creates compliance evidence bundles for violations/changes, and supports configurable remediation (notify / escalate / soft-disable). The service should integrate with the evidence/reporting automation pipeline and fit within Private/Dedicated/Hosted deployment constraints.
background: We already ingest SCIM events and produce entitlement snapshots for periodic reviews, and the evidence pipeline can assemble artifacts on-demand. However, gaps remain: (1) residency-aware rules are not consistently applied at grant-time or post-hoc; (2) evidence bundles for access reviews are manual; (3) there is no automated remediation flow for time-bound privileged access discovered outside jurisdictional policies. This ticket addresses a narrowly scoped service to close these gaps and feed outputs to the existing attestation/export workflows.
technical_design:
High-level: 1) Permission Sweeper service (idempotent) that consumes: a) SCIM change stream (delta events), b) periodic entitlement snapshots, c) SAML/SSO login metadata for proof-of-access. 2) Residency engine evaluates rules: tenant residency tags, region allow-list, product-surface exceptions. 3) Violation lifecycle: detect -> enrich (context: who, when, last auth, role scope) -> classify (policy type: residency/retention/privilege-duration) -> action (notify custodians / create evidence bundle / auto-revoke temporary grants). 4) Evidence bundle: signed JSON manifest + relevant logs (SCIM diff, RBAC snapshot, login traces), stored encrypted in evidence S3 with retention policy and index entry in evidence catalog. 5) API: read-only endpoints for Console + webhook/event sink for downstream automations.

Implementation notes: - Use existing SCIM consumer library and reuse entitlement snapshot table. - Residency metadata is stored in Tenant metadata service (add a small residency cache with TTL). - Evidence bundle format follows existing attestation schema but adds a "permission_provenance" section and a deterministic signature (KMS-based HMAC). - Remediation actions are gated by a policy engine with feature flags per deployment (hosted vs private).
tasks: Design residency rule DSL and map to tenant metadata fields
Build Permission Sweeper service: event consumer, evaluator, actioner
Add residency cache and TTL-backed refresh from Tenant Metadata Service
Implement evidence bundle assembler + KMS HMAC signing integration
Expose read-only API and two webhook destinations (compliance inbox, oncall webhook)
Add feature-flag gating for auto-revoke in Private/Dedicated vs Hosted
Add E2E test harness: simulated SCIM deltas + login traces to validate bundles
Update Console to show sweeper findings and link to evidence bundle
acceptance_criteria: Permission Sweeper consumes SCIM deltas and entitlement snapshots and evaluates residency rules without dropping >0.1% of events
Findings contain required provenance (actor, timestamp, SCIM delta id, last-login id) and are exported as an evidence bundle signed by KMS
Console shows sweep results and links directly to the evidence bundle with access controls enforced
Configurable remediation supports: notify-only, escalate (create ticket), and soft-disable (mark binding inactive) behind a feature flag
Automated E2E tests validate policy classification for at least 6 residency scenarios (in-region, cross-region, exception, expired-temporary-grant, orphan-service-account, delegated-access)
No P0 incidents in 72 hours after rollout to a canary tenant group
comments: 2025-03-05 Miguel Ortega: Initial design spike completed. Residency DSL proposal attached in Confluence (see links). Moving to implement core evaluator next.
2025-03-07 Aisha Patel: QA/Compliance flagged that evidence bundles must include the original SCIM change payloads with retention metadata — added to acceptance criteria.
2025-03-10 Miguel Ortega: Implemented sweeper skeleton and wired SCIM consumer in staging. Observed ~0.02% duplicate deltas — added idempotency key logic.
2025-03-12 Compliance (J. Huang): Requested explicit retention durations for evidence bundles per jurisdiction — captured in risks/mitigation below. Scheduled review 2025-03-14.
risks: Evidence bundles may contain PII/identifiers that increase retention surface and legal exposure
Auto-revoke could impact customer availability if a policy is overly broad
KMS signing across private/on-prem deployments requires different key management patterns (HSM vs cloud KMS)
High event volume tenants may create many findings and increase storage costs
risk_mitigation: Apply data minimization to evidence bundles: redact user identifiers except UID and hash of email where required
Gate auto-revoke behavior behind a tenant opt-in feature flag and require explicit approval for production canaries
Abstract KMS provider interface so Private deployments can plug HSM or customer-managed KMS; add fallback unsigned-but-audited mode
Add rate-limits and batching for findings; provide retention-tier configurations and cost estimates in Console
qa_plan: Unit tests for residency DSL parser and evaluator
Integration tests: SCIM delta -> sweeper -> evidence bundle assembly -> KMS signature validation
Chaos test: simulate duplicate/late SCIM events and validate idempotency
UAT with Compliance team using 3 sample tenants (EU, US, APAC) to validate jurisdictional retention behavior
monitoring: Alert: >1% of events dropped in 5m window
notes: This ticket intentionally scopes to detection + evidence bundle generation + gated remediation. Full access-request workflow (self-service revocations, approval UIs) will be follow-up work.
Coordinate with Privacy to finalize redaction policy before GA.
Schedule security review with Cryptography team for KMS/HSM patterns (2025-03-18).
